info.title: Snajp CRM API
info.description:
Read and write the companies and people a Snajp customer keeps in Snajp CRM, and sync a customer
register in from another system.

**Authentication.** Send the key in `X-API-Key`. Keys are created under CRM, Developers, and carry
scopes: `crm:las` (read), `crm:skriv` (write), `crm:synk` (sync), `crm:admin` (connections).

**Idempotency.** Any POST accepts `Idempotency-Key`. Within 24 hours the same key and body return
the stored response, with `Idempotent-Replayed: true`.

**Pagination.** Lists return `next_cursor`. Pass it as `cursor` until it is `null`.

**Rate limit.** 600 requests per minute and customer. `X-RateLimit-Remaining` is on every
response; a 429 carries `Retry-After`.

**Errors.** `{"detail": {"code", "message", "meddelande"}}`. `code` is stable, `message` is English,
`meddelande` is Swedish.

**Swedish formats.** Organisation numbers are checked with the Luhn digit and stored as
`NNNNNN-NNNN`. Phone numbers are stored as E.164, Swedish postal codes as `NNN NN`, dates as ISO 8601.

**Keeping a copy in sync.** Read `GET /changes` from your last `next_cursor`: one feed for every
object, in order. Or have Snajp call you: register a webhook under `/webhooks`. Listing with
`sort=updated&include_deleted=true&updated_since=<your last sync>` works as before. Deleted
records carry `deleted_at` and must be removed on your side as well.

**Webhooks.** Each delivery is a POST with `X-Snajp-Signature: t=<unix time>,v1=<hex>`, where `v1`
is HMAC-SHA256 over `"{t}.{body}"` with the webhook's secret. Answer 2xx within ten seconds.
Anything else is retried seven times over about a day.

get.summary: Everything that has changed, in order
get.description:
One feed for every object. Each write has a sequence number; read until
the list is empty and keep `next_cursor`. Asking again with the same
cursor returns only what has happened since. An event says which record
and which fields changed: fetch the record to get the values.

post.summary: Sync a batch of companies in one call
post.description:
The short way in: one batch, in the source system's own format, is one
completed run. Records are matched on the source's id, then on organisation
number, so sending the same batch again changes nothing.

postal_code.title: Postal Code
postal_code.description: Postal code. Swedish codes are stored as `NNN NN`.

org_number.title: Org Number
org_number.description: Swedish organisationsnummer. `556036-0793`, `5560360793`, `16556036-0793` and `SE556036079301` are all accepted. The check digit is verified. Unique per customer: posting an existing number updates that company.

private_person.title: Private Person
private_person.description: The customer is a private person, not a company. No personal identity number is stored, and the record is always `do_not_contact`: it is left out of every send, list and Iris run.

custom.title: Custom
custom.description: Your own fields, up to 50 scalar values.

name.title: Name
name.description: Your name for the source, e.g. `hubspot`. Unique.

mapping.title: Mapping
mapping.description: Overrides on top of the system's default mapping, per object and target field. See GET /connections/systems for the defaults and the format.

missing_records.title: Missing Records
missing_records.description: What a completed full sync does with records the source no longer has.

include_private_persons.title: Include Private Persons
include_private_persons.description: Off by default: records the source marks as private persons are skipped (`reason: privatperson`). Turn it on to store them, marked `private_person` and `do_not_contact`.

email.title: Email
email.description: Unique per customer: posting an existing address updates that person.

company_id.title: Company Id
company_id.description: Id of a company in Snajp CRM.

legal_basis.title: Legal Basis
legal_basis.description: GDPR article 6 basis for holding the person.

mapping.title: Mapping
mapping.description: Try a mapping without saving it.

url.title: Url
url.description: A public https address. Required when creating.

events.title: Events
events.description: Event types to receive, e.g. `company.updated`. `*` (the default) is all of them. GET /webhooks/events lists them.

active.title: Active
active.description: Turning a disabled webhook on again resets its failure count.
